body.heading: A jar for the good days
paragraphs: A gratitude jar is the simplest family ritual there is: an empty jar, a stack of small slips of paper, and a pen kept beside it. Whenever something good happens — a kind word, a funny moment, a meal that turned out right, a stranger who helped — someone writes it down and drops it in.

Nothing is too small. "Dad made pancakes" counts exactly as much as "I passed my exam." The jar is not a diary and it is not homework; it is a collection of proof that good things happened, even on ordinary days.

body.heading: Opening it together
paragraphs: Pick a day to open the jar: New Year's Eve, a birthday, the first day of a holiday, or simply the last Sunday of the month. Take turns pulling out slips and reading them aloud, and let the memories do their work — the room will fill with laughter and "I'd forgotten that!" faster than you expect.
Then start again with an empty jar. A family that keeps a gratitude jar ends up with two things: a jar full of good days, and a habit of noticing them while they are happening.

description: An empty jar, some paper slips and a pen — the simplest family ritual there is. Catch the good moments as they happen, then open the jar together and remember them all.

safetyNotes: Keep the jar somewhere stable and out of reach of very small children if it is glass — or use a sturdy plastic jar instead.
supervision: An adult starts the jar and joins in; children write their own slips, with help reading or writing if needed.
takeaway: Write down one good thing whenever it happens, and at the end of the month you'll hold a jar full of proof that the good days were real.
